title: Extending a prescribed inverse and homotopy across a base simplex
statement:
Use arbitrary-base cartesian fibrations, natural markings and relative sharp mapping complexes as in [lem-coef-relative-marked-anodyne-calculus], and quasicategory equivalences as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $n\geq1$, let $X	o\Delta^n$ and $Y	o\Delta^n$ be small cartesian fibrations, and let $f:X^
atural	o Y^
atural$ be a marked map over $\Delta^n$ whose vertex-fiber maps $f_i:X_i	o Y_i$ are equivalences of quasicategories for $0\leq i\leq n$. Put $X_\partial=X	imes_{\Delta^n}\partial\Delta^n$ and $Y_\partial=Y	imes_{\Delta^n}\partial\Delta^n$ with pulled-back markings, and write $f_\partial$ for the restriction. Suppose a marked map $r_\partial:Y_\partial^
atural	o X_\partial^
atural$ over $\partial\Delta^n$ and an edge $h_\partial:r_\partial f_\partial	o\operatorname{id}_{X_\partial}$ in $\operatorname{Map}^\sharp_{\partial\Delta^n}(X_\partial^
atural,X_\partial^
atural)$ are specified.

There exist a marked map $r:Y^
atural	o X^
atural$ over $\Delta^n$ and an edge $h:rf	o\operatorname{id}_X$ in $\operatorname{Map}^\sharp_{\Delta^n}(X^
atural,X^
atural)$ whose restrictions to the boundary are exactly $r_\partial$ and $h_\partial$, respectively. No inverse or homotopy on the interior is part of the hypotheses; the extension is relative to the given boundary data.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.3.5, proof (3) implies (2), simplex case with specified boundary inverse and homotopy; the proof uses Corollary 2.4.4.4 and Proposition A.2.3.1 Read from HTT-second-reading.pdf in the delivery sandbox; no Stacks tag states this simplicial result. Not archived in project literature/.

proof.text: Write $S=\Delta^n$, $A=X_\partial$, $B=Y_\partial$, $p:X\to S$ and $q:Y\to S$. The nerve of the ordered category $[n]$ is a quasicategory: an inner horn specifies its ordered vertices and therefore its unique simplex. Thus $X,Y$ are quasicategories by the relative cartesian-fibration calculus. Pullback to any face $\tau:\Delta^k\hookrightarrow S$ is cartesian, with exactly the pulled-back natural marking; its total spaces $X_\tau,Y_\tau$ are again quasicategories. The map $f_\tau$ preserves cartesian edges and has the given fiber equivalences at its vertices. Work in the Joyal model structure throughout the unmarked part of this proof; all simplicial sets are cofibrant since the empty inclusion is a monomorphism.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.3.5, simplex reduction; preliminary quasicategory and marking checks.

proof.text:
For each face $\tau$ and vertices $x,z\in X_\tau$ over $s,t$, compare $\operatorname{Map}_{X_\tau}(x,z)$ and $\operatorname{Map}_{Y_\tau}(f x,f z)$ over the identical Kan base $\operatorname{Map}_{\Delta^k}(s,t)$. For a vertex $\alpha:s\to t$ of that base, choose a cartesian lift $e:w\to z$ in $X_\tau$. Its image $f(e)$ is cartesian in $Y_\tau$. The natural cartesian mapping-fiber formula identifies the induced map on homotopy fibers over $\alpha$ with
$$\operatorname{Map}_{(X_\tau)_s}(x,w)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{(Y_\tau)_s}(f x,f w).$$
This is an equivalence because the given fiber functor is an equivalence and equivalences induce equivalences of mapping spaces. The homotopy-fiber detection theorem, with identity map on the base, now shows that the map of total mapping spaces is an equivalence. This includes the case when the base mapping space is empty. Hence every $f_\tau$ is fully faithful.

source.place: Corollary 2.4.4.4 and its proof, expanded using Proposition 2.4.4.2; the existing natural mapping-fiber node supplies that proposition.

proof.text: For any vertex $y\in Y_\tau$ over $s$, a quasi-inverse of the fiber equivalence supplies $x\in(X_\tau)_s$ and an equivalence $f(x)\simeq y$ in that fiber. Its inverse triangles remain inverse triangles in $Y_\tau$, so this is also an equivalence of total-space objects. Thus the full essential image of $f_\tau$ is all of $Y_\tau$. The full-essential-image theorem applied to the fully faithful functor of step 2 supplies a coherent quasi-inverse on the whole target. The Joyal quasicategory characterization makes $f_\tau$ a categorical equivalence. In particular $f:X\to Y$ is one.

Also $f_\partial:A\to B$ is a categorical equivalence; do not assume the boundary itself is a quasicategory. Prove, simultaneously for every subcomplex $T\subseteq\partial\Delta^n$, that $X_T\to Y_T$ is a categorical equivalence by induction on the finite number of nondegenerate simplices of $T$. For $T=\varnothing$ it is an isomorphism. Attach the missing faces in increasing dimension. If $T'=T\cup_{\partial\tau}\tau$, then both preimages are degreewise pushouts of the spans $X_T\leftarrow X_{\partial\tau}\hookrightarrow X_\tau$ and $Y_T\leftarrow Y_{\partial\tau}\hookrightarrow Y_\tau$. Indeed each degree is the union of the two inverse-image subsets, with intersection exactly the inverse image of $\partial\tau$. All six objects are Joyal-cofibrant; the displayed right legs are monomorphisms. The map on the face is weak by step 3, and the maps on $T$ and $\partial\tau$ are weak by induction, since those have fewer simplices. Clause (b) of the cofibrant-span comparison gives the desired weak equivalence on $T'$. A vertex attachment has empty boundary and is covered by the same argument. Take $T=\partial\Delta^n$.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.3.5, weak equivalence of the boundary mapping-cylinder comparison, with finite face gluing written out; homotopy pushout calculus A.2.4.

proof.text:
Form the unmarked simplicial pushouts
$$C=Y\amalg_{X\times\{0\}}(X\times\Delta^1),\qquad C_0=B\amalg_{A\times\{0\}}(A\times\Delta^1)\amalg_{A\times\{1\}}X,$$
and put $D=(A\times\Delta^1)\cup(X\times\{1\})\subseteq E=X\times\Delta^1$. Their evident maps to $S$ ignore the interval. The given $r_\partial,h_\partial$ and $1_X$ glue to $\psi_0:C_0\to X$: at time zero the agreement is exactly $h_\partial|_0=r_\partial f_\partial$, and at time one it is $h_\partial|_1=1_A$. Let $j:C_0\to C$, $i:D\hookrightarrow E$, $a:D\to C_0$ and $b:E\to C$ be the canonical maps. We have $ja=bi$. The map $j$ is a monomorphism even though $f$ need not be: degreewise, pushing out $X\times\{0\}\hookrightarrow E$ replaces the time-zero copy by $Y$, and $C_0$ is the subset consisting of $B$ and the image of $D$. A point of $D$ at time zero belongs to $A$, and $f^{-1}(B)=A$ because $f$ lies over $S$. Thus precisely the same identifications occur in $C_0$ and in $C$, proving injectivity.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.3.5, definition of Z and Z-prime (here C and C_0); degreewise gluing and injectivity.

proof.text: The map $a:D\to C_0$ is the pushout of $f_\partial:A\to B$ along the monomorphism $A=A\times\{0\}\hookrightarrow D$. The map $b:E\to C$ is the pushout of $f:X\to Y$ along $X=X\times\{0\}\hookrightarrow E$. The Joyal model structure has all objects cofibrant, so the all-cofibrant left-properness theorem applies to it. Steps 3 and 4 therefore make both $a$ and $b$ categorical equivalences. No right properness of the Joyal model structure is asserted or used.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.3.5, replacement by a weakly equivalent inclusion; Proposition A.2.4.2.

proof.text: There is an extension $H:E\to X$ of $\psi_0a:D\to X$ over $S$. Apply the equivalence-prism extension theorem to the inner fibration $p:X\to S$, the subset $A\subseteq X$, and terminal endpoint $\epsilon=1$, exchanging the two product factors. This subset contains every vertex of $X$ because $n\geq1$ and every vertex of $S$ belongs to its boundary. On the prism domain use $h_\partial$ on $A\times\Delta^1$ and $1_X$ on $X\times\{1\}$. At each vertex the vertical edge is an equivalence: restriction of $h_\partial$ to the corresponding vertex fiber is an edge of the sharp mapping core and hence has equivalence components in that quasicategory. Its inverse triangles remain inverse triangles in $X$. The prescribed bottom map is $p\operatorname{pr}_X:E\to S$. All domain and base agreements are exact, so the theorem gives the required $H$.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.3.5, final prism extension; Proposition 3.1.1.5. The existing vertex-containing inner-fibration prism theorem supplies this exact extension.

proof.text:
Strictify the extension across $j$ explicitly. Write $[-,-]_r$ for Joyal right homotopy classes as in the cited Mathlib leaf. Since $b:E\to C$ is a weak equivalence between cofibrant objects and $X$ is fibrant, surjectivity of $b^*$ gives a class represented by $\psi_1:C\to X$ with $[\psi_1b]=[H]$. Consequently
$$[\psi_1ja]=[\psi_1bi]=[Hi]=[\psi_0a].$$
Injectivity of $a^*$ gives $[\psi_1j]=[\psi_0]$. The single-right-homotopy criterion and the good-path-object clause represent this equality by a good right homotopy from $\psi_1j$ to $\psi_0$. Apply homotopy extension along the cofibration $j:C_0\hookrightarrow C$, with first endpoint extension $\psi_1$. The second endpoint is a map $\psi:C\to X$ satisfying $\psi j=\psi_0$ exactly. This use of the two general Mathlib leaves is the concrete homotopy-class calculation behind HTT A.2.3.1.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.3.5, strictification by Proposition A.2.3.1; Mathlib Homotopy.lean:200 and RightHomotopy.lean:183, :233, :324.

proof.text: Set $r=\psi|_Y$ and $h=\psi|_{X\times\Delta^1}$. The pushout relation gives $h|_0=rf$, and the copy of $X$ in $C_0$ gives $h|_1=1_X$; also $r|_B=r_\partial$ and $h|_{A\times\Delta^1}=h_\partial$ exactly. Although step 8 worked in the unmarked model category, $\psi$ is automatically over $S$. Indeed $C_0$ contains every vertex of $C$, so $p\psi$ and the prescribed map $C\to\Delta^n$ agree on vertices. A simplex of $\Delta^n=N([n])$ is determined by its ordered vertices, so these maps agree on every simplex. All vertical edges of $h$ are the already prescribed boundary edges since $A$ contains every vertex of $X$. They are equivalences by step 7. The pointwise-equivalence theorem makes $h$ a coherent natural equivalence from $rf$ to $1_X$ in $\operatorname{Fun}(X,X)$.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.3.5, automatic base compatibility and vertical equivalences for n>0.

proof.text: Step 9 gives a coherent natural equivalence $rf\simeq1_X$. Apply the cancellation lemma [lem-coef-infinity-equivalence-cancellation] to the categorical equivalence $f$ and this equivalence. It makes $r$ a categorical equivalence; hence the Joyal characterization supplies a coherent quasi-inverse, and the functor-equivalence clause gives that $r$ is fully faithful and essentially surjective.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.3.5, marking check: cancellation of $f$ using $rf\simeq1_X$ and Joyal characterization.

proof.text: Put $E=Y^{\mathrm{op}}$, $F=X^{\mathrm{op}}$, $B=S^{\mathrm{op}}$, $T=r^{\mathrm{op}}$, $p_0=q^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $q_0=p^{\mathrm{op}}$. Opposites are quasicategories by clause (4) of the relative-cone equivalence node. Reversal of the vertex order takes inner horns to inner horns and final horns to initial horns. Therefore $p_0,q_0$ are inner fibrations and every $q$-cartesian edge $e$ gives a $p_0$-cocartesian edge $e^{\mathrm{op}}$. Reversing the quasi-inverse and its two inverse triangles from step 10 makes $T$ a functor equivalence. The equality $pr=q$ from step 9 gives $q_0T=p_0$ strictly. These statements use only order reversal and the cited definitions; no preservation of markings by $r$ has yet been assumed.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.3.5, marking check; Proposition 2.4.4.3 on opposites.

proof.text: Fix a $q$-cartesian edge $e$ of $Y$ and use the notation of step 11. Its opposite is $p_0$-cocartesian. The image-test comparison lemma [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-image-criterion], applied to the fully faithful functor $T=r^{\mathrm{op}}$ over $B$, says that for every test vertex $z\in E$ the cocartesian criterion square for $T(e^{\mathrm{op}})$ at $Tz$ is a homotopy pullback. The lemma uses the coherent Hom transformation and the whole-square commutation data, not only four edge homotopy classes.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.4.3 (dual), image-test mapping-square comparison in the marking check of Proposition 3.1.3.5.

proof.text: The equivalence $T$ is essentially surjective by step 10. Therefore every test vertex $w\in F$ is the endpoint of an equivalence $u:Tz\to w$. Apply the essential-image transport lemma [lem-coef-infinity-equivalence-preserves-cocartesian-edges] to this $u$ and the image-test pullbacks from step 12. Coherent postcomposition by $u$ and by its base image, together with the inverse-edge and composition homotopies, gives an equivalence of whole criterion squares; homotopy pullback invariance transfers the property to the square at $w$.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.4.3 (dual), transport of the mapping-square criterion from essential-image test vertices to arbitrary test vertices.

proof.text: The cocartesian mapping criterion [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] now applies to $T(e^{\mathrm{op}})$ at every test vertex, so it is $q_0$-cocartesian. Reversing the initial-horn condition back across opposites gives that $r(e)$ is $p$-cartesian. Since $e$ was arbitrary, $r:Y^\natural\to X^\natural$ preserves the natural marking.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.4.3 and Proposition 3.1.3.5, reversing the cocartesian criterion and horn indices.

proof.text: Finally $h$ is a marked map $X^\natural\times(\Delta^1)^\sharp\to X^\natural$. For a cartesian edge $e:x\to x'$ and a constant interval edge, its image is $rf(e)$ or $e$, which is cartesian by step 14. For the interval edge $0\to1$, consider the product triangle with vertices $(x,0),(x',0),(x',1)$. Its first edge maps to $rf(e)$, which is marked, and its second to the prescribed vertical edge at $x'$, also marked because it comes from $h_\partial$. The third edge is exactly $h(e,0\to1)$. The marked triangle generator (iii) and the relative lifting criterion force this third edge to be marked: the underlying 2-simplex is already fixed, so lifting against the marking-addition generator changes no simplex. This covers every marked edge of the product, including degenerate $e$. By the definition of the relative sharp mapping complex, this marked cylinder is the required edge $h:rf\to1_X$, with its exact boundary restriction from step 9.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.3.5, upgrade to the required marked homotopy; Definition 3.1.1.1(3) and Remark 3.1.1.10.
